notes: ACCESS: plain direct fetch worked throughout via the shared probe.py session - no proxy, no curl_cffi profile sweep needed, matching the prior Home-Decor pass. Note macys.com/robots.txt is itself 403 to us on every route tried (direct, Googlebot UA, r.jina.ai); the only body I could get was translate.goog's OWN robots.txt (the documented trap), so I could neither confirm nor refute a Claude-specific directive - I saw no evidence of one, and /shop/* pages serve normally. All non-/shop paths (robots.txt, every sitemap.xml variant, /navigation/header-footer) return the same Akamai Access-Denied page, so the sitemap route was unavailable. SCOPE: stayed strictly inside the Furniture department, macys.com/shop/home/furniture-mattress?id=29391 (h1 'Furniture', categoryName 'Furniture & Mattresses', 65,527 items). The assigned roster URL /shop/home?id=22672 still normalises to the Home landing id=173142; Furniture is its child department. Did not enumerate the rest of the department store. TREE: the global mega-menu only exposes 2-3 levels, but every category page carries its own left-rail child list, so I crawled recursively - a node's children are the links whose path is exactly the current path plus one lowercase slug segment (facet URLs are distinguishable because their added segment is Capitalised, e.g. /Brand/..., /Bed_style/..., /Pageindex/...). That produced 136 real category nodes to depth 3. Depth 4 was probed and does not exist. This found 40+ nodes the mega-menu never shows (e.g. Armoires, Vanities, Room Dividers, Buffets & Sideboards, China Cabinets & Curios, Wine Racks, Hall Trees, Shoe Racks, Loveseats, Modular Couches, Curved Sofas, Swivel Chairs, Loft Beds, Montessori Beds, the whole Outdoor sub-tree).
